observation.description: An accept list containing text/plain is effectively unusable: finalization detects the content type from bytes, and plain text detects as application/octet-stream, so a text file uploaded under a { mediaTypes: ['text/plain', ...] } intent refuses at finalize with SNAPBACK_ASSET_MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED ('detected content type application/octet-stream is outside the intent's accept list'). The intent authoring layer accepts the declaration without warning. This arm switched its fixture to a PDF (magic-detectable) to proceed.

competitorOutcome.description: Frozen storage arms trust declared content types (with their own risks); Snapback's detect-from-bytes is the safer design but needs either a text detector or a generation-time refusal of undetectable accept entries.

mustNotRegress: Detection-from-bytes as the authority over declared content types.
smallestCoherentFix: Detect valid UTF-8/ASCII text as text/plain (bounded sniff), or refuse at generation any accept entry the detector can never produce, naming it.
acceptanceWitness: A .txt upload under a text/plain intent finalizes ready, or the intent refuses at generation with a named diagnostic.
